note: Doors that write and admit a caller carrying no credential, outside /v1/federation/* (which check:federation-signatures owns and asks a sharper question about: owner-gated, or the peer's Ed25519 signature verified in the handler). Triaged 2026-09-04. AN ENTRY HERE IS NOT DEBT. All forty were read one at a time — twelve of them in docs/internal/n2-triage-avoimet-kirjoitusovet.md, whose numbers this gate reproduces exactly — and none is a hole: every one is gated inside its handler by a credential the middleware scanner cannot see, or is a door where no session can exist yet by construction. That is a different result from the route-scope backlog and worth saying out loud. The gate exists for the forty-first door: one that writes and takes no credential is easy to add in a hurry and reads as normal afterwards, because it looks like the forty above it. Adding one is now a sentence somebody has to write.

exempt.POST /v1/admin/seed-examples: GATED IN THE HANDLER — an operator JWT, or the node admin password / admin session cookie compared timing-safely (admin.ts:612-622). 401 otherwise. The JWT is never trusted below the operator role.
exempt.POST /v1/admin/setup/auth: NO SESSION CAN EXIST YET — this IS the admin-password login. The password is compared timing-safely and the door carries the admin auth rate limit.
exempt.POST /v1/admin/setup/register: GATED IN THE HANDLER — the bootstrap door for a node with no accounts: the admin session cookie or the timing-safe admin password, which is why every owner it creates is granted the operator role.
exempt.POST /v1/admin/setup/token: GATED IN THE HANDLER — two proofs: the admin password or session, plus possession of the owner's private key checked against the stored public key before any JWT is issued.
exempt.POST /v1/agents/connect: THE CREDENTIAL IS IN THE BODY — a one-time connectivity key (OTK), consumed with a grace window. An agent presenting it has been authorized by the owner already; there is no session because this is where one is established.
exempt.POST /v1/agents/device-authorize: RFC 8628 — the device-authorization request. optionalAuth resolves an identity and refuses nobody (invariant 6), which is correct here: the flow exists so that a device with no credential can ask for one, and the owner approves it on a second screen.
exempt.POST /v1/agents/device-token: RFC 8628 — the credential is the `device_code` issued by the step above, and a wrong grant_type is a 400. A session cannot exist: this is the exchange that produces one.
exempt.POST /v1/agents/v2/token: THE CREDENTIAL IS IN THE BODY — the v2 agent token exchange, bounded by the login rate limit. Same shape as every other token endpoint here.
exempt.POST /v1/agents/verify: THE CREDENTIAL IS IN THE BODY — `owner_token`, verified with verifyJWT inside the handler before anything is written.
exempt.POST /v1/app-grants/token: OAUTH TOKEN ENDPOINT — the credential is the authorization code plus the PKCE verifier. Requiring a session here is structurally impossible: the code IS the proof, and the client that holds it has no other.
exempt.POST /v1/apps/:owner/:filename/webmcp/to: DELEGATES TO A MEASURED CHOKEPOINT — the tool-call path decides the caller, the permission, the pacing and the price in one place. The door does no deciding of its own, which is why it carries nothing.
exempt.POST /v1/auth/anonymous: OPEN BY DESIGN — refused with 403 unless the node runs in anonymous mode, and what it mints is the node's own anonymous identity, which owns nothing. This is the door that exists so a person can look before signing up.
exempt.POST /v1/auth/refresh: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE REFRESH TOKEN — presented in the body or the httpOnly cookie and verified in the handler. optionalAuth is on the chain and gates nothing; the refresh token is the whole proof.
exempt.POST /v1/auth/revoke: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE TOKEN BEING REVOKED — ending a session must work when the access token has already expired, which is exactly when no session can be presented.
exempt.POST /v1/auth/token: NO SESSION CAN EXIST YET — the sign-in itself: an owner name plus a signature over `owner + nodeId + timestamp`, or the password door beside it. Carries the login tarpit and body validation.
exempt.POST /v1/auth/token/exchange: THE PRESENTED PAT IS THE CREDENTIAL — resolvePat verifies hash, expiry and the owner's CURRENT roles, so a revoked token stops working immediately. Rate limited by the login tier.
exempt.POST /v1/commerce/webhooks/stripe/:owner: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE SIGNATURE — Stripe signs the payload and the handler verifies it against that owner's endpoint secret before reading a field. A webhook sender cannot hold a session by definition.
exempt.POST /v1/ecosystem-apps/hello: THE FIRST HALF OF A HANDSHAKE — the principal does not exist yet. What happens here is TOFU key pinning; nothing the app claims is trusted until the owner approves it on the second half.
exempt.POST /v1/ecosystem-apps/token: DEVICE-CODE GRANT — the same shape as the agent token endpoints: the credential is the code the approved handshake issued.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii: REGISTRATION — no account exists to authenticate against. Gated by the node's registration mode (refused in 'invite' and 'closed'), the registration rate limit and body validation.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/account/recover: RECOVERY — the point is that the person cannot sign in. The credential is the recovery code mailed to the address on file; rate limited.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/login: NO SESSION CAN EXIST YET — the password sign-in. Login tarpit, rate limit and body validation, and the same refusal whether the account is missing or the password wrong.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/login/passkey/options: NO SESSION CAN EXIST YET — the first half of a passkey sign-in. It writes nothing to the database: it hands out a random challenge held in memory for sixty seconds, and reads at most one owner's credential ids. A username nobody has is answered exactly like one that exists. Rate limited at four times the login tier, because one sign-in costs two requests.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/login/passkey/verify: NO SESSION CAN EXIST YET — the passkey sign-in itself. The credential is the assertion: @simplewebauthn/server checks the signature against the stored public key, the challenge against the one this node issued, and the origin and relying party id against this node's own, all before completeOwnerLogin() reads or writes anything — which then refuses a deactivated account. Login-tier rate limit.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/login/attach-email: PART OF SIGNING IN — attaches the verified address to the account being signed into, with the login tarpit and rate limit. The credential is the sign-in in progress.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/login/saml/:id/acs: THE ASSERTION CONSUMER — the identity provider's browser POST, so no session can exist yet. The credential is the SAML Response itself: signature against the connection's pinned certificates, Audience, InResponseTo and validity window, all before any account is read or written.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/login/saml/:id/finalize: THE ONE-TIME USERNAME CHOICE — the credential is the signed, httpOnly pending-signup cookie minted by the ACS, verified for purpose, provider and expiry. Registration mode gates creation; the registration limit bounds abuse.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/magic-link: SENDS A CREDENTIAL, DOES NOT ACCEPT ONE — it mails a link to the address on file. Rate limited, and it answers the same whether the address is known.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/password/reset: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE RESET CODE — mailed to the address on file, single-use, rate limited. A person resetting a password has no session by definition.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/password/reset-request: SENDS A CREDENTIAL, DOES NOT ACCEPT ONE — same shape as the magic link.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/register-web: REGISTRATION FROM A BROWSER — no account exists yet. Registration mode, registration rate limit, body validation.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/verify-email: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE EMAILED CODE — proves control of the address, with the login tarpit and rate limit.
exempt.POST /v1/ghii/verify/eudiw/callback: THE WALLET'S CROSS-DEVICE RETURN — the credential is the OpenID4VP response, and the owner it binds to comes from the nonce recorded when the request was made rather than from anything the caller says. 503 when the feature is off.
exempt.POST /v1/intake/:org/:ws/:formId: OPEN BY DESIGN — a public intake form. Being fillable by someone with no account is the whole feature; rate limited, and what it writes lands in the workspace that published the form.
exempt.POST /v1/invitations/:token/accept: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE INVITATION TOKEN — in the path, single-use. optionalAuth is on the chain because an invitee may or may not already have an account, and it gates nothing either way.
exempt.POST /v1/organisms/:id/workspace/share/u: THE CREDENTIAL IS THE SHARE PASSWORD — a share link with a password is meant to open for someone with no account. Rate limited.
exempt.POST /v1/owners: REGISTRATION — the direct door, refused by the node's registration mode in 'invite' and 'closed'. Body validated. No account exists to authenticate against.
exempt.POST /v1/registration-invites: SELF-SERVICE INVITE REQUEST — anyone may ask; the node's registration mode refuses it in 'invite' and 'closed'. A per-IP limit on the route and a per-address limit in the service, so rotating IPs still cannot bury one inbox.
exempt.POST /v1/setup/init: FIRST RUN ONLY — an IP check, and a 403 the moment a single owner exists. The door closes itself and cannot be reopened from outside.
exempt.POST /v1/signals/:owner/:streamId/hit: A BEACON — counting a click from a person who has no account is what it is for. Rate limited per IP at 120 a minute, and it writes a counter and nothing else.
exempt.POST /v1/validate: WRITES NOTHING — a stateless schema check: it takes a body and an endpoint name and answers valid or invalid. It is in this population because the population is 'not a GET', which is the right way to draw it; this is the one member where the verb is the only thing write-shaped about it.
exempt.PUT /v1/upload/:token: THE PRE-SIGNED TOKEN IS THE CREDENTIAL — that is what presigning means. 401 when it does not verify, 409 when it has been used, 410 when it has expired.
